I've run procurement at a large European bank for twelve years, and I go to Las Vegas every autumn. Here's my rule: I never sign anything in a hotel suite. Never. Good vendors understand that. What I do in the suite is listen, ask hard questions, and nail down one next step. I always open the meeting myself. I say who we are, where we are in the decision, and what I need to learn in thirty minutes. If a vendor puts a term sheet on the table, I take it home and read it with my legal team. And if there's an exclusivity clause, I flag it on the spot. It's usually the exclusivity, not the price, that kills a deal. Finally, I tell them our decision timeline honestly. Six months is normal for us. Vendors don't love hearing that, but they respect it.

Hi Fabio, it's Dana, from the demo station yesterday. Thanks again for coming back at two thirty. My team loved your questions about legacy systems. So here's the thing: our CEO is in town until Thursday, and we'd love to invite you to our suite at the hotel tomorrow at eleven. Thirty minutes, max. We'd like to talk about a proof of concept with Bradesco. Before the meeting, could you ask your legal team about a mutual NDA? That way we can share real numbers. And, to be transparent, our CEO will probably bring a draft term sheet. No pressure at all. Just text me if eleven works for you. Thanks!
